Losses During Crystallization: To study sorbent losses during crystallization, existing glassware, including scintillation vials, round bottom flasks, and glass reactors will be used. For sorbent losses during crystallization, our experimental plan defines one equivalent cycle a fixed reaction time in the crystallizer, which has been set by our base case technoeconomic scenario. We routinely run crystallization experiments overnight, which is equivalent to more than a hundred equivalent cycles. We planned to carry out decomposition studies during Budget Period 2 with the existing experimental setup and analytical instrumentation but did not complete due to the termination of the project. Losses During Thermal Regeneration: To study sorbent losses during thermal regeneration, we have constructed a custom thermal degradation reactor, and supplemented these studies with TGA experiments. For sorbent losses during thermal regeneration, our experimental plan defines one equivalent cycle as fixed reaction time in the thermal regeneration unit, which has been set by our base case technoeconomic scenario. We first generated the BIG-CO via a standard precipitation with a loaded aqueous amino acid salt solution. 3 We isolated the BIG-CO via filtration, taking care to leave the sample relatively wet with aqueous amino 3 acid salt solution. We took half of the wet solution, and washed with DI water to remove the residual contactor solution. Using both the washed and unwashed sample, we heated small samples in vials held at 120C, with distinct samples held under either nitrogen or the air. 5 When samples were washed, no decomposition was observed after heating under normal atmospheric composition/air. Similarly, we observed no decomposition when unwashed BIG-CO3 - still containing residual contactor solution - was heated under nitrogen atmosphere, indicating that the combination of BIG- CO3 and contactor solution is heated under an inert atmosphere. However, when the unwashed BIG-CO3 sample was heated under air, decomposition products were detected via HPLC and discoloration of the sample was observed. To further supplement our investigation of decomposition during thermal regeneration, we also analyzed BIG-CO3 by an isothermal TGA method at 120C. These stability results are in agreement with the high stability of the pure BIG as observed in our thermal degradation reactor.
